title: PR stitch + unwind scratchpad
content:
Context:
This is my working scratchpad for small, high-risk PRs where we need a fast but safe path: stitch the change into main, watch behavior for 30–60m, and have an immediate unwind plan.

Why: we often have low-latency perf/kv-cache/route-fallback changes that are small code-wise but high-impact at runtime. Full canary infra is heavy for these — need a compact playbook.

Primary goals:
- Make safe merges that minimize blast radius
- Reduce time-to-rollback if things go wrong
- Ensure follow-ups (monitoring, filters, tickets) are created immediately

Quick decision matrix (before merging):
- Surface area: single package / cross-service? -> single package ok for fast path, multi-service -> require canary/A/B
- Database/Schema? -> require migration plan. Avoid fast-path merge.
- New feature flag gating? -> prefer merge behind flag
- Backwards compat? -> if not, escalate for 1:1 review

Pre-merge checklist (short):
[ ] PR description: one-line summary + list of endpoints affected
[ ] Smoke tests: local unit + 1 integration scenario recorded
[ ] Metrics hooks: increment a feature metric or ensure traces have tag
[ ] Rollforward verification script (see below) present
[ ] Revert branch created (git checkout -b revert/<pr>)

Merge commands I use (safe, local):
- git checkout main && git pull origin main
- git checkout -b merge/pr-1845 && git merge --no-ff pr-1845
- run quick smoke: ./scripts/smoke-run.sh --target=runtime-local
- git push origin merge/pr-1845 && open merge in GH

Immediate post-merge (first 30–60 minutes):
- Tag the release/merge in Slack: #deploy-alerts (include PR link + quick sanity)
- Start a short watch: 0–30m: error rate, p95 latency, 5xx count
- Check traces for new tag: route=\"runtime-stitch\"
- If any of these triple: 5xx increase > 5x baseline, p95 > baseline + 200ms, or a new error signature appears -> trigger unwind.

Unwind (fast rollback) plan:
- If immediate rollback: use the revert branch created pre-merge:
  git checkout main && git pull && git merge --no-ff revert/pr-1845 && git push origin main
- If infrastructure-level rollback needed (config/route): revert config or toggle feature-flag to off
- Post-rollback steps: roll forward a small canary with instrumentation to validate fix, and open follow-up ticket with root cause hypothesis

Heuristics for not-reverting immediately:
- Minor increase in latency but only on 2% of requests -> keep under observation 2–4 hours
- New logs appear but are sparsely sampled -> add diagnostic logging and re-evaluate

Quick tests matrix (what I run in 10 mins):
- Unit tests (fast)
- Key integration: end-to-end request for 3 payload shapes (small, medium, large)
- KV-cache warm path + cold path test (same request repeated x10)
- Fuzz-ish: random 100 requests from real trace snippet

Common failure modes I've seen:
- KV cache watermark eviction causing cold miss storm on first deploy -> mitigation: gradual cache warmup and ramped traffic
- Missing header/flag path that bypasses a fast-path -> mitigation: ensure deterministic default in code + test coverage
- Race condition in async background flush -> mitigation: short-circuit flag + metric to measure latency tail

Notes on observability to add before next run:
- Add a counter metric: pr_1845_applied{route,env} and expose in console
- Add a small trace tag: stitch_pr=1845 to make filter queries easier
- Create dashboards: short-lived watchboard template (errors, p95, qps, pr_applied)

Post-merge follow-ups (create tickets asap):
- ENG: add regression unit for the exact sequence that failed (link to trace/snippet)
- SRE: consider short-term scaling config if the change increases CPU by >10%
- Product: notify if feature toggle behavior changes UX

Housekeeping TODOs (my checklist):
- [ ] Copy this scratchpad into a short Org playbook if this flow repeats twice more
- [ ] Add automated revert job in CI that can be triggered by a tag to main
- [ ] Improve smoke script to run against the current staging cluster rather than local emulation

Small snippets / commands for reference:
- Create revert branch quickly: git branch revert/pr-1845 main && git push origin revert/pr-1845
- Fast rollback via GH: use the Revert button on merged PR — but validate generated revert locally before pushing

Open questions / unresolved thoughts:
- How to standardize the 'watch window' across teams? 30 vs 60 minutes tradeoffs. Could be policy by impact level.
- Would a lightweight canary router for single-service merges be worth the infra cost? (maybe a serverless traffic-split)
- Do we want a one-click 'soft-revert' that only disables the feature-flag instead of code revert? Need feature-flag maturity.

Scratchline (notes to self):
- If we see cold-miss storms again, try adding short-lived prefix cache warming: request top 50 keys over 5 minutes before cutover.
- Keep revert branch naming strict: revert/pr-<id>/ts-<yyyymmdd> to avoid confusion.

Recent related artifacts:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1845 (stitching kv cache checkpoint path)
- Jira: ENG-3228 (investigate runtime tail spikes)

End of scratchpad. Will iterate and move to shared playbook if stable.
